## The checker's report

Check of the Chalk Train design sheet (`chalk-train`, band 2 to 4), round 1. File: `games/chalk-train/ART.md` as checked, everything above `## The look`.

Records: all four exist. Code, standing and check state match the lookup today (us-ca 4.4 Writing: department-published-foundation, confirmed; the three nl card statements: curriculum-institute-guidance, confirmed; none is a core goal, so no regime).
Limits: every limit the sheet takes is in that record's Limits and none comes from the examples. One description of a Dutch record drops a word the record names (finding 6), and one count of code matches is wrong (finding 1).
Levels: for ages 2, 3 and 4 in both jurisdictions the levels, sub-bands, basis (us-ca official, nl convention), the end-of-primary label at nl age 4 and "no gap" are as printed. The infant-toddler reading-language lane (6 records) holds nothing on making marks, as the sheet says.

Findings

1. **"### us-ca", line 197.** The lookup by code 4.4 prints three us-ca records (Writing, Geometry and Spatial Thinking, Earth and Space Science), not four. Replace the parenthesis with:
`(us-ca code 4.4 under Strand 4.0, Writing, of Language and Literacy Development; the code alone matches three records)`

2. **"### us-ca", after line 200 (ruling 7).** The claim says which jurisdiction each part comes from, but no sentence under this heading says that two parts of the skill have no California record. Add as a new line after "Short of the record":
`  No California record is named for two parts of the skill: drawing as a way of exploring writing, and a mark that tells someone something. Those parts are taken from the Dutch records alone, and nothing is named in their place here.`

3. **"### The claim", line 233, and "Where the two differ", line 226 (ruling 1; pack: education, name-the-records-a-claim-rests-on.md; age-maps-to-levels-through-the-lookup.md).** The claim gives all three Dutch statements "for ages 2 to 4" and rests a two-year-old on "the Dutch guidance" as a whole, but the lookup returns fase 1 only at age 4. It also cites "/ 3" by code alone, and that code matches two nl records (the peuter card and the fase 1 card). Replace line 233 with:
`Chalk Train is designed from one California learning foundation for preschool and transitional kindergarten, a foundation published by the state department of education and not a standard (us-ca 4.4 under Strand 4.0, Writing, of Language and Literacy Development, its statement for the earlier age only; confirmed), from which it takes only that scribble comes before any letter, for ages 3 and 4; from two statements of the Dutch curriculum institute's content card for peuters (nl Oriëntatie op geschreven taal / 7 and / 3, both under Aanvankelijk schrijven of the peuter card; both confirmed), from which it takes exploring writing through drawing and scribbling, and experiencing that a mark can tell someone something, for ages 2 and 3 and for a child who has only just turned four; and from one statement of its content card for fase 1 (nl Voorbereidend schrijven / 4; confirmed), from which it takes writing with the child's own drawings and scribbles, for age 4. The Dutch statements are guidance and not law. For a two-year-old it is designed from the two peuter statements alone. The marks are made with a finger and no tool, no kind of stroke is named by any of these records, and the game shows no letter. It says nothing about what any child can do.`
Replace line 226 with:
`- **Age.** The Dutch peuter statements are returned for ages 2 and 3 and for a child who has only just turned four, and the fase 1 statement for age 4. The California lane for age 2 holds no record on making marks, and the foundation used is for ages 3 and 4. For a two-year-old the game follows the two Dutch peuter statements alone.`

4. **"Where the two differ", line 229 (ruling 6).** The Standing point does not say which jurisdiction the game follows. Replace with:
`- **Standing.** One is a foundation published by a state department; the others are guidance from the curriculum institute. Neither is a standard or the law, and the sheet treats them as unrelated statements. The game follows each for its own part only: the claim calls the foundation a foundation for what is taken from California, and calls the guidance guidance for what is taken from the Dutch cards.`

5. **"The representation", line 69 (pack: education, two-jurisdictions-are-never-equated.md; ruling 7).** "The records below carry this as…" gives all the records what only the Dutch ones carry, and "finding out" is stronger than the record's word, which its Limits gives as experiencing. Replace the paragraph with:
`**The idea.** Before a child writes, the child makes marks: dots, lines, wiggles, rounds and scribbles, made for their own sake and then made to tell someone something. The Dutch records below carry this as exploring writing through drawing and scribbling, and as experiencing that a mark can tell something; the California record carries only that scribble comes before letters.`

8. **"The object-by-action grid", line 46, against line 20 (pack: game-design, ages-2-to-4.md; hidden-never-counted.md).** Line 20 names a rider's home as a thing the child aims at, but the grid's "six things it can land on" has no home, so a mark on a pond, nest, leaf or cushion has no stated answer. Add at the end of line 46:

With the whole screen as the drawing surface, "a second finger draws a second line" turns a resting wrist into chalk that pushes the child's marks past the cap. Replace with:
`- No pinch, tilt, shake, double tap or long press. One finger draws at a time: another finger or a resting palm is ignored, draws nothing, and never ends the line being drawn.`

11. **"The scenes", line 181, against lines 21 and 141 (ruling 5; By age, quantities).** As written, a run of `two-at-once` layouts puts two riders at home, two in play and two waiting on the tar. That is six riders and four stops, against the stated cap of four riders, three stops and `riders: at most four`. Replace the sentence "When that cycle begins … on the tar." with:
`When that cycle begins, the rider after it is drawn in at its stop, and earlier homes are rubbed away with their riders' waves until only the home reached last is left. Of a layout with two riders only the first waits ahead on the tar; the second is drawn in at its stop when that cycle begins. So there are never more than four riders (two of the layout in play, one waiting, one at home) and three stops on the tar.`

12. **"The designed order", lines 118 and 114, against lines 128 and 181 ("How a cycle restarts").** "From the second cycle on" contradicts lines 128 and 181, which draw the next rider in when a cycle begins, and it leaves the first ending with nobody waiting. "Carry both at once" also cannot work if only `two-at-once` has two wagons. Replace line 118 with:

The train has two wagons at every position, so while a wagon is free the child may fetch the waiting rider before taking the current rider home and carry both at once. It is farther away, so it looks like more, and it is never asked for.`
